MMI raises $125 million to expand Symani robotic microsurgery

The Series D supports commercial expansion and clinical evidence generation, following approximately 50 installations and 3,500 reported procedures.

Medical Microinstruments / GlobeNewswire ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Financing commercial growth

Medical Microinstruments announced a $125 million Series D on October 8. BioStar Capital led the round, joined by S3 Ventures, Angelini Ventures, an unnamed strategic corporate investor and existing investors. The funding supports expansion in the United States and other key markets, as well as clinical outcomes research.

Supporting delicate surgical work

Symani supports open soft-tissue microsurgery through wristed microinstruments, tremor reduction and motion scaling. MMI reports approximately 50 installed systems and 3,500 complex procedures worldwide. Those adoption figures are company-reported totals, not comparative evidence that the platform outperforms other surgical methods.

Evidence for future applications

MMI plans further clinical work, including REMIND, alongside instrument and digital capabilities. References to Alzheimer’s research describe evidence being developed, rather than an established treatment benefit. Adoption totals and outcomes for a specific clinical indication remain different measures and should be assessed separately.
